subject: Rerank pilot recap + proposed canary playbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@brightcart.co>, Jamal Ortiz <jamal@brightcart.co>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rerank pilot recap + proposed canary playbook

Hi Elena / Jamal —

Thanks again for the hour today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

Summary from discovery:
- BrightCart sees inconsistent ordering on category + search pages for long-tail queries; product team suspects current lexical scorer underweights recency signals.
- Success metrics: increase top-10 relevance (business-defined NDCG@10) and measurable uptick in add-to-cart rate for search-driven sessions.
- Constraints: PII must not leave BrightCart environment; model must be deployable in your VPC (you flagged compliance needs).

What Redwood recommended on the call:
- Run a small reranking pilot using our lightweight reranker (redwood/rerank-lite-v2) on a production-sampled shard of logs (<= 1M queries).
- Benchmark against your current baseline using NDCG@10 and MRR; surface per-category deltas to catch regressions.
- Canary plan: 5% traffic for 2 weeks, hold regular checkpoints.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Please share a 7–14 day sample of search logs (query, candidate set, click/conversion labels) — secure link or S3 with restricted role works.
2) Confirm which metric (NDCG@k vs business CTR) should be primary for go/no-go.
3) Any blacklisted queries/categories we should exclude from evaluation?

I've attached the prompt_set_v1.jsonl we discussed (example reranker prompts and feature schema) and a draft playbook (canary_playbook.pdf). Dev will follow up with preliminary benchmark numbers once we have a sample.

Next steps: if you can share the sample by EOD May 13 we can target a pilot kickoff the week of May 18.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Rerank pilot recap + proposed canary playbook

Thanks, Soojin — great summary. A few clarifications from BrightCart side:

- We can provide a redacted 14-day sample with session IDs, queries, candidate product IDs, click indicator, and order value. We'll deliver to an S3 bucket with a temp role.
- Primary metric: business prefers NDCG@10 (aligned to revenue-weighted lifts), but we'll watch CTR/ATC as secondary.
- Privacy: we need assurance that any artifacts or derived features that leave our VPC will be hashed/pseudonymized; we cannot share raw customer emails or PII.

Timeline looks good — aiming to have sample ready by May 13. Two Qs: 1) how quickly can Redwood produce baseline vs reranker numbers once we hand over data? 2) If we see small regressions in niche categories, will Redwood provide per-category analysis to inform fallbacks?

Elena Park
Head of Search & Personalization, BrightCart
elena@brightcart.co

Date: 2026-05-10T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rerank pilot recap + proposed canary playbook

Elena / Jamal —

Thanks for confirming. A few technical notes and preliminary numbers from our local dry-run on a public-ish benchmark (to set expectations):

Dry-run results (representative only):
- Baseline (BrightCart lexical mimic): NDCG@10 = 0.622, MRR = 0.403
- redwood/rerank-lite-v2 (reweighted recency + learned interactions): NDCG@10 = 0.657 (Δ +0.035), MRR = 0.428 (Δ +0.025)
- Observed small negative delta for one coarse category ("Home Decor") where NDCG@10 dropped by ~0.012 — this aligns with sparse click labels and noisy relevance signals.

Proposal for evaluation + canary:
1) Preprocessing: Redwood will only store hashed IDs and aggregated features when operating outside your VPC. All raw logs remain in your S3.
2) Offline eval: we'll compute per-category NDCG@10 and MRR; produce a regression heatmap (CSV attached: rerank_ndcg_results.csv).
3) Canary: 5% traffic routing to reranker for 14 days. Monitor: NDCG@10, MRR, CTR, ATC (add-to-cart) and a small sample of session-level revenue. Guardrail: if any category shows >0.02 absolute NDCG@10 regression AND material revenue drop, we auto-roll back.
4) A/B measurement plan: use stratified sampling by device and query length, run sequential hypothesis testing with early-stopping criteria.

Operational asks from BrightCart: give us a path to 1) deploy model variant in your VPC (we have a private deployment package) or 2) grant a restricted compute staging environment if you prefer Redwood-hosted testing with hashed artifacts.

Links: offline evals and full CSV are at https://drive.redwood.com/brightcart/rerank-pilot-2026 (read-only).

We can turn around baseline+rerank offline numbers within 48 hours after you hand over the sample. If you want per-category deep dives we'll need an extra 24–48 hours.

—
Dev Patel
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Canary playbook and rollback criteria (for AE to confirm with customer)

Team — looping to finalize ops steps so Soojin can lock in dates with BrightCart. Draft playbook highlights:

- Canary percentage: 5% of search traffic (split evenly across device segments).
- Duration: 14 days with daily automated metric checks and a mid-run checkpoint at day 7.
- Metrics & thresholds: primary NDCG@10 (relative uplift target >= +0.02 for pass), hard rollback if any category shows <= -0.02 absolute NDCG or > -5% conversion delta.
- Rollback procedure: immediate traffic shift to baseline + artifact collection; post-mortem within 3 business days.
- Communication: weekend freeze for canary launches; on-call SE + AE alerted at metric breach.

Attachments: canary_playbook.pdf (ops steps), runbook snippets for model rollback. Soojin — confirm with BrightCart whether May 18 start works and whether they want Redwood-hosted (hashed artifacts) or VPC private deployment.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Rerank pilot recap + proposed canary playbook

All — we reviewed the playbook internally and we're good to proceed.

- We'll upload the redacted 14-day sample to the S3 bucket tonight and send the temp role by tomorrow morning.
- Primary metric confirmed: NDCG@10 (revenue-weighted).
- Agree to a May 18 kickoff for 5% traffic canary. We will need a short contract addendum on data handling and rollback SLAs — can your legal team share a template?

Thanks, looking forward to the numbers.
